title: Company-wide policies and process documentation
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

This document consolidates Redwood Inference's company-wide policies and standard operating procedures for: access & permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expenses, vendor management, travel policy, and internal document templates. It is intended as the canonical reference for employees and managers. Where specialized guidance exists (security, legal, finance), this page links to the authoritative policy and callout sections.

Scope

- Applies to all Redwood employees, contractors, and approved vendors with access to Redwood systems or representing Redwood in business activities.
- Covers corporate (G Suite, Slack, HR systems), infrastructure (cloud accounts, consoles), and product-facing systems (internal admin tools, dashboards).

Owner and Governance

- Owner: People Ops (primary), with delegated ownership for technical controls to Security and Eng Infra.
- Review cadence: annual review by People Ops + Security + Finance; ad-hoc updates for regulatory or tooling changes.
- Escalation: unresolved disputes escalate to Head of People Ops.

1) Access & Permissions

Principles:
- Principle of least privilege: grant the minimum access needed for job function.
- Role-based access: prefer role groups over individual grants.
- Time-bounded access: temporary access should have explicit expiration.

Process for access requests:
1. Employee or manager submits an Access Request via the IT Service Portal with reason, required resources, and expected duration.
2. Request routed to the owning team (e.g., Eng Infra for cloud, Data Security for analytics) for approval.
3. Approver validates justification, assigns role/group, and sets an expiration date when appropriate.
4. Access is provisioned by IT/IAM automation and logged in the access audit table.

Offboarding:
- HR triggers automated deprovisioning on termination or role change. Critical accounts (admin, production deploy keys) require manual verification by Security and Eng Infra.
- Deprovision checklist: revoke console/API keys, remove from group memberships, reclaim licenses, close vendor access.

Periodic review and audit:
- Quarterly role reviews for critical systems (cloud, production databases, SSO admins).
- Annual company-wide access audit. Exceptions must be documented with owner and compensating controls.

2) Change Management

Purpose:
- Ensure predictable, reversible changes to production and critical infrastructure with minimal customer impact.

Change categories:
- Emergency: immediate mitigation for incidents; retrospective RFC required within 48 hours.
- Standard: pre-approved, low-risk changes executed via automation (e.g., routine configuration updates).
- Non-standard (Major): architectural or risky changes that require scheduled maintenance windows and full review.

Change request workflow:
1. Submit RFC (Request for Change) in the Change Management system with scope, risk assessment, rollback plan, test plan, and stakeholders.
2. Triage by Change Advisory Board (CAB) — includes Eng Infra, Eng SRE, Security, Product — within 3 business days for non-emergency changes.
3. Approvals: minor standard changes may have automated approvals; major changes require CAB sign-off and scheduled maintenance window.
4. Execute change using runbooks and automation; capture deployment artifacts and verification steps.
5. Post-change verification and monitoring for at least 24 hours.
6. Postmortem for any change that causes degradation or outages.

Change windows and communications:
- Production maintenance windows are scheduled Saturdays 02:00-06:00 PT for lower-impact changes; Major rollouts require notification 7 days in advance.
- Customer-impacting work: product & CS must approve communication plans.

3) Data Management

Goals:
- Protect sensitive data, ensure compliance with retention policies, and provide reliable data lifecycle processes.

Classification:
- Public: content safe for public consumption.
- Internal: non-sensitive internal company data.
- Confidential: PII, customer data, security-sensitive information.
- Restricted: regulated data or data subject to contractual obligations.

Storage and handling rules:
- Confidential and Restricted data must be stored in approved systems with encryption at rest and in transit.
- Access to Confidential/Restricted data requires explicit IAM groups and documented business justification.
- Backups: production data backups retained according to the backup schedule (default 90 days for general datasets; 7 years for finance/ legal records unless otherwise required).

Retention and deletion:
- Data retention schedules are defined by data class and business need.
- Automated retention policies will delete or archive data per schedule; requests for exceptions need approvals from Data Owner + Legal.

Data incident response:
- Follow the Incident Response playbook under security-and-compliance/incident-response-security.
- Notify Data Protection Officer (or legal) within 72 hours for incidents involving regulated personal data where applicable.

4) Procurement and Expenses

Principles:
- Competitive pricing, budget ownership, and approvals aligned with delegation of authority.

Procurement workflow:
1. Raise a Purchase Request in the Procurement system with cost center, justification, and proposed vendor.
2. Finance validates budget and approves if within threshold. Higher-value purchases require VP or CFO approval per the financial approval matrix.
3. Procurement team negotiates contracts and issues Purchase Order (PO).
4. Receiving and invoice process: validate delivery, match invoice to PO, and process via Accounts Payable.

Expenses and reimbursements:
- Employees submit expenses via the Expenses system within 30 days of spend.
- Required receipts for all card charges; corporate cards reconciled monthly.
- Per-diem and travel rates follow the Travel policy section below.

Approval matrix (summary):
- Up to $1,000: Manager
- $1,001-$10,000: Director
- $10,001-$50,000: VP
- >$50,000: CFO approval and Procurement involvement

5) Vendor Management

Vendor selection and onboarding:
- Vendors classified by risk: Low, Medium, High. Security and Legal must review Medium/High risk vendors.
- Standard onboarding checklist: contract with data protection clauses, insurance certificates, background checks where relevant, confidentiality agreement, and assigned internal owner.

Ongoing vendor oversight:
- Quarterly business reviews for strategic vendors; annual security posture reviews for vendors that handle Confidential or Restricted data.
- Maintain a vendor inventory with owner, contract end date, data access scope, and renewal reminders.

Offboarding vendors:
- Revoke access, collect equipment, and ensure secure deletion of company data. Confirm with Vendor Manager and Legal that retention obligations are met.

6) Travel Policy

Booking and approvals:
- Travel should be booked through the approved travel vendor/portal. Managers must pre-approve business travel and confirm budget.
- Employees should choose economy class for flights < 6 hours; business class requires VP approval.

Expenses and per-diem:
- Meals reimbursed up to $75/day domestic; $100/day international standard unless pre-approved. Alcohol reimbursed when part of business meals and within per-diem.

Safety and insurance:
- Company provides business travel insurance for approved trips. Employees must register international travel with People Ops for evacuation alerts and assistance.

Health and sustainability:
- Encourage combined trips and virtual-first options when feasible to reduce travel carbon footprint.

7) Internal Templates and Artifacts

This section lists the canonical templates available to employees. Templates are stored in the company templates library (link in related pages). Common templates include:
- Access request form (IT Service Portal template)
- Request for Change (RFC) template for CAB submissions
- Vendor onboarding checklist
- PO request template for Procurement
- Travel approval and expense report templates
- Incident report and postmortem templates

Template governance:
- Template owners are responsible for keeping templates up-to-date. Templates include a header with owner and last review date.

Appendix: Quick reference tables

Access provisioning SLA:
- Standard role provision: target 1 business day
- Elevated/privileged access: target 3 business days with approval
- Emergency access: approved same-day via emergency escalation

Change classification summary:
- Emergency: immediate (retrospective RFC)
- Standard: low-risk, automated approvals
- Major: CAB review and scheduled window

Procurement approval matrix (as above): see Procurement and Expenses section for thresholds.

Contacts and escalation list

- People Ops (policy owner): people-ops@redwood.ai
- Security (technical controls): security@redwood.ai
- Procurement and Finance: procurement@redwood.ai; finance@redwood.ai
- Vendor Manager: vendors@redwood.ai
